dedupe_keys.name: what a waste global database what a waste 3 0

description: The What a Waste Global Database aggregates statistics on solid waste management from around the world and underpins the World Bank Group's What a Waste 3.0 report, the third edition after 2012 and 2018. It covers 217 countries and economies and 262 cities across the whole waste value chain: waste generation and composition, collection coverage, treatment and disposal (landfill, open dumping, incineration, recycling, composting), waste workers, legal and institutional arrangements and the management of plastic waste, with projections to 2050 under different policy choices. The World Bank compiles it from official statistics and published public-sector data, and where those are missing from international organisations, development agencies and academic journals; every source and estimate is noted. Coverage is global at country and city level, from 2010 with projections through 2050, mostly as annual values. Access is free from the World Bank Data Catalog as city-level and country-level Excel files with codebooks (updated 11 March 2026) and through the catalogue's API service and Data360. Licence: Creative Commons Attribution 4.0. Caveats: definitions and reporting quality differ between countries and cities, many values are single-year snapshots from different years, and the World Bank notes that individual data points vary while general trends should hold. Simulation uses: capacity planning of collection, treatment and landfill infrastructure and scenario analysis of future waste loads. Related: waste system models such as SwolfPy (catalogued as model-swolfpy) need generation and composition inputs of this kind.
